newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-DLR/MARK END UNDER 1.8680 MAY CHEER BULLS.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-DLR/MARK END UNDER 1.8680 MAY CHEER BULLS.

text.p: Dollar/mark's pullback on Thursday is unlikely to signal long-term damage and may instead provide bargain-buying opportunities as low as 1.8550, chartists said.

"(The dollar) would have to close below 1.8680 marks to confirm the move down to 1.8550. Then, you buy it there because it's going to rocket to 1.92," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
Dollar/mark's retreat from a peak of 1.8913 on Wednesday -- the fourth near eight-year highs in as many sessions -- is expected to be relatively shallow and brief.
The area around 1.8575, the low on Tuesday, is expected to contain the dollar/mark downside for now and may even be somewhat of a stretch of how far this correction should go, experts said.

"I don't think there is any reason to think the uptrend is over," said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International. "If we head back above 1.8730/40, that would be somewhat encouraging for a test back above 1.88 by tomorrow."
But a break below 1.8575 marks would be the first negative signal that 1.8910 is in fact going to hold as the dollar's high for a while, Grant said.
Meanwhile analysts said bull strategies should remain in force for dollar/yen as well, with the zone of strong support between 117.50 to 118 being a good bet for buyers.
Above the near three-month high at 119.58 yen, set on Wednesday, comes minor resistance at 120 and 120.50 yen.
Chartists expected new highs eventually around 121.50, assuming the 117.40 yen prop from the July 31 low holds.
"We continue to focus on short-term buying strategies," Grant said.
In late afternoon trading on Thursday, dollar/yen was at 118.45/50, up from 118.39/44 at the open.
Dollar/mark was quoted at 1.8675/85, down from 1.8755/60.
